c.tagline: Colonial highland city amid pine forests and Maya villages

taxi.fareNote: Unmetered taxis charge fixed in-town fares (roughly $30-50 MXN); agree on the price before getting in

emergency.note: 911 is Mexico's national emergency number; the historic center has good response, outlying villages less so

avoid.reason: The city itself has no no-go zones, but avoid driving rural Chiapas highways at night due to informal roadblocks and occasional unrest in outlying villages.
Watch for pickpockets in the Mercado Municipal and on unlit streets late at night, and use ATMs inside banks.

hood_desc: The heart of San Cristóbal, centered on the leafy Plaza de la Paz and its 16th-century cathedral. Cobblestone streets are lined with colonial buildings now housing cafes, galleries, and artisan shops. Most major sights, including the Santo Domingo church and the Na Bolom cultural center, are within walking distance.

A pedestrian-only street running east from the main plaza, packed with restaurants, bars, and live-music venues. It's the liveliest strip after dark, popular with backpackers passing through the Chiapas circuit. By day it doubles as a shopping street for amber jewelry and textiles.

A hillside neighborhood east of downtown, capped by the Templo de Guadalupe and its long staircase with panoramic valley views. Quieter and more residential than the center, with a small daily market at the foot of the steps. A good sunset spot away from the crowds.

Home to many of the city's textile and amber workshops, where Maya artisans sell handwoven huipiles and silver jewelry. The streets are narrower and more local than the tourist core. Good for browsing craft markets at a slower pace.

A traditional, working-class barrio on the northern edge of downtown, centered on its own small colonial chapel. Far fewer tourists venture here, giving a glimpse of everyday local life. Quiet in the evenings with simple family-run comedores.
lodging: Hotel Parador San Juan de Dios

water.note: Drink bottled or purified water; tap water is not potable.

transit.map: no formal transit map; informal combi routes
transit.note: The historic center is entirely walkable; colectivos and taxis connect outer neighborhoods and nearby villages like San Juan Chamula

air: Ángel Albino Corzo International Airport, Tuxtla Gutiérrez (TGZ)
bus: OCC/ADO buses to Tuxtla Gutiérrez, Palenque, Oaxaca, and Mexico City

tip.r: Tipping 10-15% at restaurants is standard; round up for taxis; tip guides on tours
